purpose: Project layout and runtime boundary policy for Python Headless Web as the default product and Electron as an optional shell.

remote_publish.role: Remote-published source is the minimal executable product surface, not the full local development workspace.
rules: tests/ must remain local-development-only and must not be tracked in remote-published source.
Remote-published source must keep the program executable with all supported features available.
Build outputs, smoke workspaces, generated caches, and local runtime data remain excluded.
Default clone users run Python Headless Web without npm, Electron, or Docker.
Remote-published source excludes local development tests while preserving a runnable product surface.
Electron is an optional shell around the same Python backend and Remote Web UI.
The canonical Remote Web source is app/web/remote.
Legacy PyQt6 Desktop source is removed from active source ownership.
Legacy PyQt6 Desktop can be inspected through git history only, never through default launchers.
Cleanup/delete candidates must be recorded before destructive source cleanup.
Round 9 cleanup is complete only as a non-destructive candidate inventory until explicit delete approval is granted.
Clone-user Web execution and Electron release shell packaging are separate tracks over the same backend and same Remote Web source.
Active refactor plans must include gate setup, implementation, modification, deletion, verification, post-work evaluation, and commit handling.
